examples.en: I was so shocked that I fainted on the spot.

examples.ko: 더운 날 오래 서 있던 학생이 기절했어요.
examples.en: A student who had been standing for a long time on a hot day fainted.
Some people pass out when they see blood.
I almost fainted, but I barely held on.
My friend suddenly passed out, so we called an ambulance.
The movie was so scary that I wanted to pass out.

explain: 실제로 쓰러졌을 때보다 '놀라서 기절할 뻔했어요'처럼 과장해서 말할 때가 더 많아요. 병원이나 뉴스에서는 '의식을 잃다', '쓰러지다'를 더 자주 써요. '졸도하다'도 있지만 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 써요.
explain_en: Koreans use it more often as an exaggeration, as in 'I almost fainted from shock' (기절할 뻔했어요), than for real fainting. In hospitals and the news, 의식을 잃다 (lose consciousness) and 쓰러지다 (collapse) are more common. 졸도하다 also exists but is rarely used in daily conversation.

en: be well versed in; be knowledgeable about

examples.en: That teacher is well versed in Korean history.
I asked a friend who knows computers inside out for help.

examples.ko: 그는 동네 맛집에 정통해서 어디든 추천해 줘요.
examples.en: He knows the local restaurants so well that he can recommend anywhere.

examples.ko: 저는 요리에 정통하지 않아서 레시피를 봐요.
examples.en: I'm not an expert at cooking, so I follow a recipe.
He is a professor with a reputation for knowing this field thoroughly.
He is well known for being an expert on Korean movies.

explain: '~에 정통하다'처럼 '에'와 함께 써요. 어떤 분야를 깊이 아는 사람을 칭찬할 때 쓰는 격식 있는 말이라서, 친구끼리는 '~를 잘 알아요'라고 더 많이 해요. '능통하다'는 외국어나 기술을 능숙하게 쓸 때 써요(영어에 능통하다).
explain_en: It is used as '~에 정통하다', with the particle 에. It is a fairly formal way to praise someone who knows a field deeply; friends more often just say '~를 잘 알아요'. 능통하다 is different: it is for being fluent in a language or skilled at using a technique (영어에 능통하다).

examples.en: Abusing a child is punished by law.
A person who abused animals appeared on the news.
If a parent abuses a child, you have to report it.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 직원을 학대한다는 소문이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a rumor that the company mistreats its employees.

examples.ko: 누구도 약한 사람을 학대해서는 안 돼요.
examples.en: No one should mistreat a weaker person.
I saw a video of someone abusing a cat and reported it.

explain: 힘이 약한 사람이나 동물에게 몸과 마음의 상처를 주는 심각한 일에 써요. 가볍게 놀리는 정도에는 안 써요. 당한 쪽은 '학대를 당하다', '학대받다'라고 해요. '괴롭히다'보다 훨씬 무겁고 법과 뉴스에 자주 나오는 말이에요.
explain_en: It refers to serious harm done to the body or mind of someone weaker, such as a child or an animal, and is not used for light teasing. The victim is described as 학대를 당하다 or 학대받다. It is much heavier than 괴롭히다 (to bother, bully) and often appears in law and the news.

examples.en: Please mix the flour and milk well.

examples.ko: 페인트 두 가지를 혼합하면 새로운 색이 나와요.
examples.en: If you mix two paints, a new color appears.
It's a juice blended from several ingredients.
This music blends tradition and modernity.

examples.ko: 세제를 혼합해서 쓰면 위험할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Mixing cleaning products can be dangerous.
Mix the two doughs and wait 30 minutes.

explain: 요리책·설명서·과학 글에 자주 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 '섞다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. '밥에 나물을 섞어 먹어요'처럼요. '혼합물'(mixture), '혼합복식'(mixed doubles)처럼 합친 말로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It appears often in recipes, instructions and science writing, while in everyday talk 섞다 sounds much more natural, as in '밥에 나물을 섞어 먹어요'. It also shows up in compounds such as 혼합물 (a mixture) and 혼합복식 (mixed doubles).

examples.ko: 누에는 고치를 만들고 그 안에서 변해요.
examples.en: A silkworm spins a cocoon and changes inside it.
I watched a moth come out of its cocoon.
Silk is woven from thread drawn from silkworm cocoons.

examples.ko: 아이가 하얀 고치를 손으로 만져 봤어요.
examples.en: The child touched a white cocoon with their hand.

examples.ko: 애벌레는 고치 안에서 몇 주를 보내요.
examples.en: The caterpillar spends several weeks inside the cocoon.
The cocoon split open and a moth came out.

explain: '누에고치'로 가장 많이 만나요. 나방 같은 곤충이 번데기를 감싸려고 실로 만든 집이에요. 나비는 보통 '번데기'만 말해요. 동사 '고치다'(to fix)와 소리가 비슷하니 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: You will meet it most often in 누에고치 (silkworm cocoon). It is the thread case an insect such as a moth makes around its pupa; for butterflies people usually just say 번데기 (pupa). Do not confuse it with the verb 고치다 (to fix), which sounds similar.

en: monopolize; hold exclusively; have all to oneself

examples.en: That company monopolizes the market.

examples.ko: 동생이 리모컨을 독점해서 채널을 못 바꿔요.
examples.en: My little brother hogs the remote, so I can't change the channel.
Give up the idea of keeping all the popularity to yourself.

examples.ko: 한 나라가 자원을 독점하면 가격이 올라요.
examples.en: If one country monopolizes a resource, prices go up.
That singer swept the music charts.
You can't keep all the good seats for yourself.

explain: 시장·권력·기회 같은 큰 것에도 쓰고, 리모컨·대화·인기 같은 일상의 작은 것에도 써요. 혼자만 가지려는 느낌이 강해서 부정적일 때가 많아요. '독차지하다'는 일상 대화에서 더 흔하고, '독점하다'는 뉴스와 경제 글에서 더 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It works for big things such as markets, power and opportunities, and for small everyday things such as the remote, a conversation or popularity. It often carries a negative feeling of keeping everything to yourself. 독차지하다 is more common in daily talk, while 독점하다 appears more in news and economics.

examples.ko: 관광객이 여러 곳으로 분산되어 덜 붐볐어요.
examples.en: The tourists spread out to several places, so it was less crowded.
We divided up the work, so the burden was spread out.

examples.ko: 주의가 분산되면 공부가 잘 안 돼요.
examples.en: When your attention is scattered, studying doesn't go well.

examples.ko: 투자가 한곳에 몰리지 않고 분산되는 게 안전해요.
examples.en: It's safer when investments are spread out rather than concentrated in one place.

examples.ko: 비가 와서 모여 있던 사람들이 분산됐어요.
examples.en: Because of the rain, the crowd that had gathered dispersed.
Connections are being distributed across several servers.

explain: '주의가 분산되다', '위험이 분산되다', '인구가 분산되다'처럼 추상적인 것에 자주 써요. 반대말은 '집중되다'예요. 사람이 일부러 나누면 '분산하다', 저절로 흩어지면 '분산되다'예요. '흩어지다'는 훨씬 가볍고 일상적인 말이에요.
explain_en: It is often used with abstract things: 주의가 분산되다 (attention is scattered), 위험이 분산되다 (risk is spread), 인구가 분산되다 (the population is dispersed). Its opposite is 집중되다. When someone does it on purpose it is 분산하다; when it happens by itself it is 분산되다. 흩어지다 is a lighter, everyday word.

examples.ko: 투자를 여러 곳에 분산하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's better to spread your investments across several places.
The company distributed the work among the teams.

examples.ko: 위험을 분산하려고 주식과 예금을 같이 해요.
examples.en: To spread the risk, I hold both stocks and savings.
They admitted the visitors in smaller groups.

examples.ko: 힘을 한곳에 모으지 않고 분산하면 약해져요.
examples.en: If you scatter your strength instead of focusing it, it gets weaker.
Someone suggested spreading the event dates out.

explain: '위험을 분산하다', '힘을 분산하다', '업무를 분산하다'처럼 짝으로 자주 써요. 반대말은 '집중하다'예요. 사람이 의도해서 나누는 것은 '분산하다', 저절로 흩어지는 것은 '분산되다'로 구별해요.
explain_en: Common pairings are 위험을 분산하다 (spread the risk), 힘을 분산하다 and 업무를 분산하다 (distribute the work). Its opposite is 집중하다. Use 분산하다 when someone spreads things out on purpose, and 분산되다 when things spread out by themselves.

en: oversee; supervise; be in charge of

examples.en: This department oversees the school events.
City Hall is in charge of the city's traffic.
The director oversees the entire hospital.
Do you know who is in charge of this?

examples.ko: 한 사람이 모든 업무를 관장하기는 어려워요.
examples.en: It's hard for one person to oversee all the work.
That committee was in charge of writing the exam.

explain: 기관이나 높은 자리의 사람이 어떤 일을 책임지고 맡을 때 쓰는 격식 있는 말이에요. '담당하다'는 실무를 맡는 느낌이고, '관장하다'는 전체를 총괄하는 느낌이에요. 뉴스와 공문에서 주로 보고, 일상 대화에서는 '맡다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is a formal word used when an organization or a person in a high position takes responsibility for a whole area of work. 담당하다 feels like handling the practical tasks, while 관장하다 feels like overseeing everything. You mostly see it in news and official documents; in daily talk people say 맡다.

examples.en: A cold usually comes with a cough.

examples.ko: 이 약은 졸음이 동반되는 경우가 있어요.
examples.en: This medicine can be accompanied by drowsiness.
Success has to come with effort.
If a fever comes with it, please go to the hospital.
Risk came along with the big investment.
The dizziness, together with a headache, has continued for several days.

explain: 'A에는 B가 동반되다'처럼 A와 B가 함께 따라온다는 문장에서 써요. 증상·위험·책임 같은 말과 자주 짝이 돼요. 사람이 같이 가는 '아이를 동반하다'와 달리, 사물이나 현상이 주어일 때는 '동반되다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is used in sentences like 'A에는 B가 동반되다', where B follows along with A, and it often pairs with words such as symptoms, risk and responsibility. When a person goes along with someone, as in 아이를 동반하다, the active 동반하다 is used; 동반되다 takes things or phenomena as its subject.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 은행 계좌와 연계되어 있어요.
examples.en: This app is linked to a bank account.

examples.ko: 학교 수업이 실제 일과 연계되면 더 재미있어요.
examples.en: Classes are more fun when they are tied to real work.

examples.ko: 두 사건이 서로 연계된 것 같아요.
examples.en: The two incidents seem to be connected.
Services that link up with transit cards are increasing.
This program is tied to job placement.

examples.ko: 카페 앱과 연계되고 나서 주문이 편해졌어요.
examples.en: Ordering got easier after it was linked to the cafe's app.

explain: 서비스·제도·수업·정보처럼 서로 다른 것이 이어져 함께 움직일 때 써요. 사람 사이의 관계에는 잘 안 써요. '관련되다'는 그냥 관계가 있다는 느낌이고, '연계되다'는 실제로 이어져 작동한다는 느낌이 강해요. 광고와 안내문에서 많이 봐요.
explain_en: It is used when separate things such as services, systems, classes or information are tied together and work as one. It is rarely used for relationships between people. 관련되다 only means there is some relation; 연계되다 stresses that things are actually connected and working together. You see it a lot in ads and notices.

examples.en: They link schools and companies to run practical training.
The hospital works in connection with the local welfare center.
If you link the shopping app to your card, you get a discount.
It is an activity that ties the lesson to daily life.

examples.ko: 다른 팀과 연계하려면 먼저 연락해야 해요.
examples.en: To coordinate with another team, you need to contact them first.

examples.ko: 두 서비스를 연계하는 방법을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: We're looking for a way to link the two services.

explain: 'A를 B와 연계하다'로 써요. 사람이나 기관이 일부러 이어 붙인다는 느낌이에요. 저절로 이어지면 '연계되다'예요. '연결하다'가 선·길·전화처럼 실제로 잇는 말이라면, '연계하다'는 제도·서비스·수업 같은 추상적인 것에 더 어울려요.
explain_en: It is used as 'A를 B와 연계하다', and the subject is a person or organization that links things on purpose. When the link happens by itself, use 연계되다. 연결하다 is for physically joining things like lines, roads or phone calls, while 연계하다 suits abstract things such as systems, services and classes.

examples.ko: 그 결정을 다시 한번 재고해 주세요.
examples.en: Please reconsider that decision once more.
We decided to rethink the plan.
I'm reconsidering the purchase because of the price.
It's so certain that there's no need to reconsider.

examples.ko: 회의에서 이 정책을 재고해야 한다는 의견이 나왔어요.
examples.en: At the meeting, some said this policy should be reconsidered.
I wish you would rethink the business trip schedule.

explain: 회의·메일·뉴스에서 결정이나 계획, 제안을 두고 자주 나오는 격식 있는 말이에요. 부탁할 때는 '재고해 주시기 바랍니다'처럼 공손하게 써요. 소리가 같은 명사 '재고'(창고에 남은 물건)와 헷갈리지 마세요. 친구에게는 '다시 생각해 봐'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a formal word that comes up in meetings, emails and the news about decisions, plans and proposals. When making a request it is used politely, as in '재고해 주시기 바랍니다'. Do not confuse it with the noun 재고 (stock left in a warehouse), which sounds the same. With friends you would say '다시 생각해 봐'.

examples.en: I'll set the schedule after discussing it with the team.
We're negotiating the contract terms with the company.
Please talk it over with your parents first.

examples.ko: 가격을 협의하면 조금 깎아 줄 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If you discuss the price, they might lower it a little.

examples.ko: 두 나라가 무역 문제를 협의하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The two countries agreed to hold talks on trade issues.
We reached a conclusion after thorough consultation.

explain: '~와/과 협의하다'로 써요. 서로 의견을 내며 결정에 이르는 과정이 들어 있어서 일방적인 통보와는 달라요. '상의하다'는 가까운 사람과 고민을 나눌 때, '협의하다'는 회사·기관·공식 자리에 더 어울려요. '의논하다'는 그 중간이에요.
explain_en: It is used as '~와/과 협의하다' and includes the process of exchanging opinions to reach a decision, so it differs from one-sided notification. 상의하다 fits sharing a worry with someone close, while 협의하다 suits companies, institutions and official settings. 의논하다 sits in between.

examples.ko: 정부는 피해를 입은 주민들을 구제하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The government decided to give relief to the affected residents.
We help neighbors in need with donations.
It's a system that helps people struggling with debt.
A charity began fundraising to help the refugees.
No one could save him from his situation.

examples.ko: 나라가 어려운 가정을 구제해서 생활이 나아졌어요.
examples.en: The state helped struggling families, and their lives improved.

explain: '피해자를 구제하다'처럼 정부나 단체가 어려운 사람을 도울 때 쓰는 무거운 말이에요. 개인이 친구를 돕는 일에는 '도와주다'가 자연스러워요. '구하다'는 목숨을 위험에서 건진다는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It is a heavy word, used when a government or organization helps people in difficulty, as in 피해자를 구제하다 (provide relief to victims). When an individual helps a friend, 도와주다 is the natural choice. 구하다 has a stronger feeling of saving a life from danger.

examples.ko: 사고를 낸 사람이 피해를 배상해야 해요.
examples.en: The person who caused the accident has to pay for the damage.
The company compensated the customer for the loss.
I'll pay for the window I broke.
The court ruled that the hospital must compensate the patient.

examples.ko: 배달 중 망가진 물건은 업체가 배상해요.
examples.en: The company pays for items damaged during delivery.
If you make up for the damage, I'll forgive you.

explain: 남의 잘못으로 생긴 피해를 돈으로 갚을 때 쓰고, 사고·계약·소송에서 자주 나와요. '보상하다'는 적법한 일로 생긴 손실을 갚을 때, '배상하다'는 잘못으로 생긴 손해를 갚을 때 써요. 일상에서 물건 값을 물을 때는 '물어주다'도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is used when paying money for harm caused by someone's fault, and often appears in accidents, contracts and lawsuits. 보상하다 is for making up a loss caused by a lawful act, while 배상하다 is for damage caused by a wrongful act. In daily life, 물어주다 (to pay for what you broke) is also very common.

examples.en: I'm hurt because a friend I trusted betrayed me.

examples.ko: 동업자에게 배신당한 뒤로 사람을 잘 못 믿어요.
examples.en: Since my business partner betrayed me, I can't trust people easily.
Anyone gets angry when they are betrayed.
He felt that his family had betrayed him.
I couldn't share my true feelings for fear of being betrayed.

examples.ko: 또 배신당하고 싶지 않아서 거리를 뒀어요.
examples.en: I didn't want to be betrayed again, so I kept my distance.

explain: '배신하다'를 당한 쪽에서 말하는 형태예요. 믿음을 깬 사람은 '배신하다', 상처 입은 사람은 '배신당하다'를 써요. '뒤통수를 맞다'라는 생생한 표현도 있어요. 연인이나 친구 사이의 큰 감정이 담겨 있어서 가벼운 일에는 안 써요.
explain_en: This is the form you use from the side of the person who was betrayed. The one who broke the trust does 배신하다, and the one who was hurt is 배신당하다. There is also the vivid expression 뒤통수를 맞다 (get stabbed in the back). It carries strong feelings, so it is not used for minor things.

examples.ko: 친구를 배신하는 일은 절대 하지 않을 거예요.
examples.en: I will never betray a friend.
He broke his promise and betrayed his colleague.

examples.ko: 나를 배신한 사람을 아직 용서하지 못했어요.
examples.en: I still haven't forgiven the person who betrayed me.
I practiced hard so as not to let down their expectations.
Once you betray someone, it's hard to win back trust.

examples.ko: 왜 나를 배신해서 이렇게 힘들게 해요?
examples.en: Why do you betray me and make me suffer like this?

explain: 사람뿐 아니라 '기대를 배신하지 않는 맛'처럼 기대나 믿음에도 써요. 믿음을 깨는 센 말이에요. '속이다'는 거짓말로 믿게 만드는 것이고, '배신하다'는 믿음 자체를 저버리는 거예요.

phrases.en: to betray someone who trusted you
phrases.nuance_ko: 믿던 사람이 갑자기 배신할 때 써요. 실제로 머리를 때리는 게 아니에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone you trusted suddenly betrays you; nobody is actually hit on the head.

explain_en: It is used not only for people but also for expectations and trust, as in '기대를 배신하지 않는 맛' (a taste that doesn't let you down). It is a strong word for breaking trust. 속이다 means making someone believe a lie, while 배신하다 means abandoning the trust itself.

examples.en: The scientists' cloning of a sheep is famous.

examples.ko: 이 파일은 복제해서 다른 컴퓨터에 넣었어요.
examples.en: I duplicated this file and put it on another computer.

examples.ko: 허락 없이 책을 복제하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not copy a book without permission.

examples.ko: 그림을 똑같이 복제하는 데 한 달이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a month to reproduce the painting exactly.
I went to a key shop to have a key duplicated.
Someone cloned my card information.

explain: 파일, 열쇠, 그림, 생물처럼 원본과 똑같은 것을 하나 더 만들 때 두루 써요. '복사하다'는 종이나 파일을 빠르게 베끼는 일상적인 말이고, '복제하다'는 똑같은 것을 새로 만든다는 무거운 느낌이에요. 허락 없이 하면 법 문제가 돼서 뉴스에도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is used broadly for making one more exact copy of an original, such as a file, a key, a painting or a living thing. 복사하다 is the everyday word for quickly copying paper or files, while 복제하다 feels heavier, as if creating an identical new thing. Doing it without permission can be a legal problem, so it often appears in the news.

examples.en: His face flushed when he heard the compliment.
The singer went up on stage with a flushed face.

examples.ko: 발표 때문에 긴장해서 제 볼이 상기되어 있었어요.
examples.en: I was nervous about the presentation, and my cheeks were flushed.
Her face flushed and her speech got faster.

examples.ko: 화가 나면 얼굴이 쉽게 상기되는 편이에요.
examples.en: My face tends to flush easily when I get angry.

examples.ko: 뜨거운 방에 오래 있으면 얼굴이 상기되기도 해요.
examples.en: Your face can also flush if you stay in a hot room for long.

explain: '얼굴이 상기되다', '볼이 상기되다'처럼 얼굴과 함께 써요. 부끄럽거나 흥분하거나 열이 올라 얼굴이 붉어질 때 써요. 소리가 같은 '상기하다'(떠올리다)와 다른 말이에요. 일상에서는 '빨개지다'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is used with the face, as in 얼굴이 상기되다 or 볼이 상기되다, when the face turns red from embarrassment, excitement or heat. It is a different word from 상기하다 (to recall), which sounds the same. In daily speech 빨개지다 (to turn red) is used more often.
